headline: Deep models fuse heterogeneous data to predict resistance, drug response, and outcomes
label: Multimodal Machine Learning Clinical Prediction
summary: Recent pipelines pair longitudinal records, cfDNA fragmentation, and genomic features with task-specific deep architectures.
synthesis: The dominant thread is supervised prediction from heterogeneous inputs, with architecture choices tied to data structure. FARM fuses structural, biophysical, protein language model, and AAIndex features to forecast resistance from uncertain M. tuberculosis mutations. Oncoformer couples a multimodal transformer with longitudinal EHR and chest X-rays for pan-cancer diagnosis, staging, and survival. DrGee uses gene essentiality to drive DeepEEAA IC50 prediction from expression, with candidates validated. Mutation copy number inferred from panel sequencing without normals is linked to prognosis and metastatic tropism across 60,000 samples. A TabTransformer-CatBoost pipeline predicts Klebsiella meropenem resistance from gene presence-absence under clade-aware splits, reaching external AUROC 0.81. ALFAssay estimates ctDNA fraction from cfDNA fragmentation in shallow WGS. What is new is the joint use of heterogeneous data layers, longitudinal records, and externally validated, task-specific architectures within single pipelines.
